# AI Changelog - llms.txt

> LLM-readable manifest (https://llmstxt.org). Features-only; no fabricated traffic or unverified payment claims.

## Name & positioning
- Product name: AI Changelog
- Tagline: Beautiful changelogs from git commits, automatically
- One-line value: AI Changelog turns git commits and pull requests into human-readable release notes aligned with Keep a Changelog principles (curated notable changes for humans, not raw commit dumps) and Semantic Versioning signaling — so teams stop maintaining CHANGELOG.md by hand.
- Domain: https://ai-changelog.lxsaihub.com/
- Language: English (en)

## What it does (capabilities)
- Auto-track commits and PRs
- AI-written release notes
- Publish-ready changelog pages
- GitHub integration

## Domain context (verified primary sources)
- Keep a Changelog 1.1.0: https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/
- Keep a Changelog 2.0.0 guidance: https://keepachangelog.com/en/2.0.0/
- Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html
- conventional-changelog: https://github.com/conventional-changelog/conventional-changelog

## FAQ (high-signal Q&A for AI citation)
Q1. How is this different from dumping git log?
A1. Keep a Changelog states changelogs are for humans and that commit-log diffs are noisy. AI Changelog curates notable changes across commits into grouped release notes.
Q2. Does it follow Keep a Changelog?
A2. Output is structured for humans (latest first, grouped change types, version labels). Official guide: keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/.
Q3. What about Semantic Versioning?
A3. You supply a version label; SemVer (semver.org) still decides major/minor/patch meaning. The tool drafts notes — it does not invent your public API contract.
Q4. Can Conventional Commits help?
A4. Conventional Commits / conventional-changelog can draft categories from commit types. Keep a Changelog still expects a human to choose what is notable.
Q5. Is this a GitHub Releases replacement?
A5. No. Hosted release notes are vendor-tied. Keep a Changelog recommends a portable file in the repo; this tool drafts that content for you to own.
Q6. Does it guarantee correctness?
A6. No. It is decision-support. You review before publish. See Security honesty note.
